_: Which beads under an epic are its family. `bd set-state` files its audit record as an `event` bead under the bead it changed, with a dotted child id, and `bd children` returns it - but an event is never a child. That rule reached main broken three times, each time fixed in one implementation only (cb-z330, cb-cng9, cb-u64g), so every implementation answers this table: tests/work-beads.sh, tests/verifier-epic-candidates.sh, tests/sweep-epics.sh and model::tests::the_epic_family_table_is_answered in fleet-view/src/model.rs. `under` is everything bd files under the epic, as `bd children` returns it. The three expectations are stated, not derived, so no reader re-implements the rule in its own test: `family` the ids that ARE children (no implementation exposes membership, so every reader checks only whether it is empty; the ids say which beads count, for the reader of a row); `family_closed` true when the epic has a family and every member is closed; `last_child_closed_at` the newest `closed_at` in the family, or null. An element carrying this `_` key is a comment and is skipped by every reader.

name: an unsplit epic with one state change is still childless
a closed epic whose only bead under it is an event is childless
an event newer than the last real child does not make the last close fresh
an open event does not hold back a family whose children are all closed
a closed event does not close a family whose real child is open
an epic with nothing under it is childless
two real children and no event: the newer close is the last
